speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of polycythemia vera, and have you experienced any headaches, visual disturbances, or a burning sensation in your hands or feet? REQUEST TEST: JAK2_Mutation_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the thrombocytosis and negative JAK2 test, I need to rule out other myeloproliferative disorders like essential thrombocythemia. REQUEST TEST: CALR_Mutation_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since JAK2 and CALR mutations are negative, I need to check for the third common mutation associated with essential thrombocythemia. REQUEST TEST: MPL_Mutation_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the standard myeloproliferative mutations are negative, I need to investigate other causes for your thrombocytosis, such as chronic inflammation or iron deficiency. Do you have any history of chronic infections, autoimmune diseases, or symptoms of heavy menstrual bleeding? REQUEST TEST: Iron_Study

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum Iron: Decreased; Iron Saturation: Decreased; Serum Ferritin: Decreased; Total Iron Binding Capacity: Increased

speaker: Doctor
text: Your blood work confirms severe iron deficiency, which explains the reactive thrombocytosis and your fatigue. Do you experience heavy menstrual bleeding or have any signs of gastrointestinal bleeding, such as black or tarry stools? REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your colonoscopy was normal, I need to investigate gynecological sources of blood loss. Do you experience heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Since gynecological causes have been ruled out, I suspect an upper gastrointestinal source for your iron deficiency. Do you experience any heartburn, indigestion, or abdominal pain after eating? REQUEST TEST: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy
